newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks shun Dow to close down.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks shun Dow to close down.

text.p: Mexican stocks ignored a late recovery by Dow industrials to close lower after a slow session dulled by local factors and marked by low-volume speculative trades.

"The market will stay like this for several days. It's very reluctant to undergo a greater adjustment, as we should after big gains last month we have yet to correct," said Francisco Blanco, research director at the Arka brokerage.
The leading IPC index closed 19.09 points down, or 0.58 percent, at 3,274.50. Volume was light at 52.8 million shares traded.
Dealers stressed that the IPC was very close to an important support level between 3,260 and 3,270 points.
"It came close to 3,270 points, and if we break through that level, we could quickly to fall to around 3,250 points, where bargain hunters could well step in," a floor trader said.

Both percentage gainers and losers were headed by stocks that traded at razor thin volume. Main gainer was bank stock Internal, which closed 37 centavos (5 cents) up at 3.97 pesos (53 cents) in which just 12,000 shares were traded.
Textile firm Synkro headed the losers, closing 12 centavos down (2 cents) at 1.13 pesos (15 cents), after trading just 3,000 shares.
